articles.title: Choose an AI tool by the decision it supports
articles.excerpt: Define an outcome, identify evidence and test a bounded task before adopting another AI product.

blocks.text: Start with the work, not the interface

A useful evaluation begins with a concrete job: produce a reviewed outline, locate a passage or explain a small function. Write down the input, expected output and the person accountable for accepting it. A conversational interface can serve many tasks, but that flexibility does not establish competence on your particular material. Avoid adopting a tool because a demonstration looks fluent.

items: Choose a task small enough to review completely.
Record what would make an output unacceptable, including missing evidence and data exposure.

blocks.text: Separate the application from its model

Ollama provides a model runtime; Open WebUI provides an interface that can connect to configured backends. That distinction matters because an interface is not itself model capacity or a privacy boundary. A local model, a remote provider and a connected document store can create different data paths even when the user sees the same chat screen. Map those paths before providing confidential information.
Create an evaluation you can repeat

Prepare a small set of representative questions with expected evidence. Include an ambiguous request and a question the system should decline to answer from the supplied material. Keep inputs and model settings fixed across trials. Record incorrect answers alongside useful ones rather than selecting only impressive examples.

items: Check original sources instead of grading confidence or writing style.
Treat resource use and operational effort as separate criteria from answer quality.

blocks.text: Decide what the pilot cannot prove

A small evaluation can reveal obvious failure patterns; it cannot certify reliability across every language, document or user. Document the model identifier, environment and limitations so the next reviewer can repeat the exercise. Expand only after an accountable person accepts the risks, permissions and potential provider costs.

blocks.text: Choose material you are allowed to process

Start with public guidance or a small approved document set. Do not assume that access to a file gives permission to upload it to a provider. Identify the owner, intended readers and retention policy. A pilot is easier to evaluate when its information boundary is narrow and its expected evidence is known.

items: Remove identifiers that do not help answer the task.
Confirm where documents, prompts, indexes and logs are stored.

blocks.text: Inspect the document before asking questions

Docling can convert supported documents into structured representations. Conversion is a preparation step, not proof that every table or heading survived correctly. Compare a complex page and several ordinary pages against the original. If a table lost a unit or a footnote, correct or quarantine it before using it to support an answer.
Make answers reviewable

A document workspace such as AnythingLLM can support model-backed work with a configured collection. Ask for the supporting passage alongside each answer and check it yourself. Include questions that the documents cannot answer. The correct outcome for missing evidence is a clear gap, not an invented policy.

items: Check whether restricted test users can retrieve only permitted material.
Keep an explicit unknown or escalation outcome in the task design.

blocks.text: Retain responsibility for the result

Assign a reviewer who understands the underlying work. Record which answers were accepted and why, including recurring extraction or retrieval failures. Only expand the pilot when the review cost, data controls and expected benefit justify it. No productivity gain is claimed merely because the system produced a polished paragraph.

articles.title: Plan a no-code automation before connecting live actions
articles.excerpt: Separate triggers, validation, proposals and approval to avoid turning a simple workflow into an uncontrolled side effect.

blocks.text: Describe the event and the permitted result

Write the input contract before opening a workflow builder. Identify required fields, maximum sizes and a stable event identifier. State what may happen after validation and what must remain a proposal. A request to classify a lead is not permission to send a sales message or change a contract.

items: Create representative test inputs without real customer records.
Specify a safe outcome for unknown categories and missing fields.

blocks.text: Treat the diagram as executable behavior

n8n and Activepieces provide ways to assemble connected workflow steps. Their connectors can touch real accounts, so inspect which credentials and permissions each step receives. A visually simple action may create an external record or consume a paid quota. Keep sending, deletion and payment steps disconnected during the initial design.
Test retries and duplicates explicitly

Event delivery can repeat. Store an idempotency key and decide whether another copy should be ignored, reconciled or sent for review. A failed network response does not prove that the remote action failed. Preserve uncertain outcomes rather than automatically repeating a potentially irreversible operation.

items: Test malformed payloads and unavailable dependencies.
Make failure states visible to the operator without logging sensitive payloads.

blocks.text: Approve one change at a time

Review the complete path from input to side effect with the person authorized to own it. Confirm consent, access, expected volume and a practical way to stop the flow. Enable only the smallest approved action and observe it before expanding. The existence of an AI component does not create authority to act for a customer or spend money.

articles.title: Build a research brief that survives a source check
articles.excerpt: Use AI for discovery while preserving a clear boundary between cited evidence, interpretation and unanswered questions.

blocks.text: Define the question and evidence standard

A research task needs a decision, audience and time boundary. Decide what would count as a primary source and which claims require independent corroboration. Without that standard, a generated report can accumulate links while leaving the real question unanswered.

items: Record publication dates and jurisdiction where relevant.
Separate direct evidence from marketing claims and commentary.

blocks.text: Use discovery tools as a starting point

GPT Researcher and Vane offer research or search-oriented workflows; STORM explores structured perspectives and drafting. Their outputs can suggest useful avenues, but a citation does not validate the sentence next to it. Open the source, locate the passage and read the surrounding qualifications. Do not infer a capability or legal condition from an old search snippet.
Keep an evidence table before writing prose

For each claim, record the original URL, checked date, supporting passage and any uncertainty. Note disagreements rather than silently selecting the most convenient source. If the evidence does not answer a question, keep it open. A brief that names an information gap is more useful than one that hides it behind fluent writing.

items: Check that quotations and paraphrases preserve the source meaning.
Avoid reproducing protected content beyond what your purpose and permissions allow.

blocks.text: Submit the interpretation to an editor

Build the outline from the checked evidence, then distinguish findings from recommendations. Have a reviewer inspect important claims and competing explanations. The proposed workflow has not been benchmarked here and offers no guarantee of search completeness, factual accuracy or independence from the configured providers.

blocks.text: Define the smallest useful change

A clear task names the behavior to change, the files likely to matter and the checks that will establish success. Include constraints such as preserving authorization and not adding a dependency. A request to improve a module should not become permission to rewrite infrastructure or publish a release.

items: Start from a known branch and inspect the working tree.
Write acceptance criteria that include error and permission cases.

blocks.text: Protect the execution boundary

Aider and Codex CLI support model-assisted code work through different interfaces. Review their configured model access, sandbox settings and approval behavior before supplying a repository. Code, documentation and tool output can contain instructions aimed at an agent; treat those as untrusted input rather than authority from the operator.
Review suggestions as contributions

Read every diff and requested command. Look for behavior changes hidden inside refactors, dependency updates and broad permission changes. Run the checks relevant to the modified behavior, and reproduce a suspected defect before accepting a fix. Passing compilation establishes a narrow fact, not overall correctness or security.

items: Keep credentials and restricted customer data out of prompts and fixtures.
Inspect generated migrations and destructive operations separately.

blocks.text: Preserve the normal release process

An assistant can prepare a commit, but organizational review and deployment authority still apply. Record what was tested and which uncertainties remain. If a provider call has costs, obtain an explicit budget and scope instead of assuming a coding task authorizes unlimited usage. No productivity benchmark or security certification is implied by this workflow.

articles.title: Evaluate AI analysis with independent calculations
articles.excerpt: Check extraction, transformations, units and numerical results before accepting an AI-generated explanation or chart.

blocks.text: Understand the dataset first

Identify the source, row meaning, units, time zone and missing-value policy before asking a model a question. Use a small permitted dataset with a reference total you can calculate independently. If the input is a document, verify its extraction first; a correct calculation over corrupted values is still a wrong answer.

items: Record exclusions and duplicated rows explicitly.
Do not upload personal or commercially restricted records to an unapproved service.

blocks.text: Keep generated code visible

PandasAI offers natural-language analysis interfaces, Jupyter AI connects assistance to notebooks, and LIDA explores model-assisted visualization. Each can sit inside a useful workflow, but generated code is executable input. Inspect operations, network access and file writes before running them in an appropriately isolated environment.
Verify the number and its presentation

Ask one bounded question at a time. Recalculate aggregates using a direct query or trusted analytical method and compare filters, grouping keys and rounding. For charts, inspect labels, units, baselines and the treatment of missing values. An attractive visualization can conceal a wrong aggregation or an inappropriate comparison.

items: Check denominators when presenting percentages.
Distinguish a measured observation from an estimated or model-generated result.

blocks.text: Publish uncertainty with the result

Record the data version, reviewed calculation and known limitations. A competent analyst should be able to reproduce the conclusion without relying on a model's confidence. This proposed process provides no measured accuracy improvement, and high-stakes financial or scientific decisions require the appropriate domain review.
